articles.title: The missing bow of a World War II cruiser was found 675 metres underwater, nearly 83 years after a torpedo tore it off
articles.summary: The missing bow of USS New Orleans, a US Navy heavy cruiser damaged during the Second World War, has been discovered nearly 83 years after a Japanese
articles.body: The missing bow of USS New Orleans, a US Navy heavy cruiser damaged during the Second World War, has been discovered nearly 83 years after a Japanese torpedo tore it away. The wreckage was located at a depth of approximately 675 metres in Iron Bottom Sound near Guadalcanal in the Solomon Islands on 7 July 2025.According to the US Naval History and Heritage Command, scientists and explorers aboard Exploration Vessel Nautilus used a remotely operated vehicle to examine the site after an uncrewed surface vessel identified a target during seafloor mapping. The discovery revealed the long-lost section of a warship that survived catastrophic damage during the Battle of Tassafaronga in November 1942.How scientists discovered the missing bow of USS New OrleansThe discovery was made during the Maritime Archaeology of Guadalcanal expedition, led by the Ocean Exploration Trust (OET). The team combined seafloor mapping with deepwater imaging to locate and examine the missing section of USS New Orleans.The University of New Hampshire’s uncrewed surface vessel DriX first identified a target during mapping operations. Explorers then deployed a remotely operated vehicle (ROV) to investigate the location. During a four-hour dive, archaeologists aboard the vessel and remote experts examined the wreckage in real time.They studied structural details, paintwork, and the arrangement of the anchors to establish the identity of the remains. Experts from former combatant nations also contributed to the investigation. The combined evidence confirmed that the wreckage belonged to USS New Orleans.How a Japanese torpedo tore off the cruiser's bow in 1942USS New Orleans suffered catastrophic damage on 30 November 1942 during the Battle of Tassafaronga. A Japanese Long Lance torpedo struck the ship forward of turret No. 2, detonating the forward magazines and tearing away nearly one-third of the vessel, including its bow.More than 180 sailors were killed in the blast. Despite the extensive destruction, the surviving crew carried out extraordinary damage-control efforts and ultimately saved the ship. Three sailors were posthumously awarded the Navy Cross for their actions.Despite the extensive damage, USS New Orleans managed to return to the United States under its own power, travelling stern first, for permanent repairs. The cruiser later returned to service and took part in several more campaigns before the war ended. Its survival made it one of the most severely damaged US cruisers of the Second World War to survive.Researchers use deep-sea technology to identify the lost cruiser sectionThe discovery provides an opportunity to remember the sacrifice of the crew who kept USS New Orleans from sinking after the torpedo strike. Samuel J. Cox, a retired US Navy rear admiral and director of the Naval History and Heritage Command, described the ship's survival as extraordinary given the extent of its damage.The discovery concerns a Second World War heavy cruiser, and its historical significance lies in documenting the vessel's wartime damage and survival. The expedition also demonstrates how researchers can combine mapping technology, remotely operated vehicles and expert analysis to investigate deepwater wrecks that have remained undiscovered for decades.Only 30 sunken warships have been found in Iron Bottom SoundIron Bottom Sound, near Guadalcanal in the Solomon Islands, was the site of five major naval engagements between August and December 1942. Allied and Japanese forces lost more than 20,000 personnel, along with 111 naval vessels and 1,450 aircraft, during the fighting.Only 30 of the military ships lost in the deep waters of Iron Bottom Sound had been located at the time of the announcement, leaving many others undiscovered. The search for the missing bow of USS New Orleans was part of a wider expedition led by Ocean Exploration Trust (OET) president Dr Robert Ballard.The mission brought together several partners, including NOAA Ocean Exploration, the US Naval History and Heritage Command, the Government of the Solomon Islands and the University of New Hampshire's Center for Coastal and Ocean Mapping/Joint Hydrographic Center. Representatives from Japan, Australia, and New Zealand also supported the expedition.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.body: Hundreds of Iranian fishermen have headed into the Strait of Hormuz in small boats to retrieve valuable goods, including iPhones and French perfume, from containers lost after a cargo ship sank on October 14.The Singapore-flagged GFS Pride went down after a fire broke out on board, Singapore said. All 21 crew members were evacuated safely.The vessel was carrying more than 2,500 containers when it sank, according to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) navy, which claimed the ship had entered an “unauthorised and dangerous” route and struck a sea mine, triggering the fire.Videos circulating online showed dozens of small boats moving between containers floating partly underwater. Fishermen were seen hauling boxes from the sea, while one boat attempted to tow an entire shipping container.The rush to recover cargo comes as attacks on commercial vessels in and around the Strait of Hormuz intensify amid the ongoing war. The GFS Pride was the second ship to sink within 24 hours and the third reported loss of its kind during the conflict. The Antigua and Barbuda-flagged Cape Dao sank following an attack on September 23.Iran links Hormuz reopening to US withdrawalIran on Friday said the Strait of Hormuz would reopen if the United States withdrew its forces from the region.Brig Gen Mohammad Akraminia, an Iranian army spokesman, warned that Tehran would force American troops out if they remained in the region.“If America leaves the region, the Strait of Hormuz will open, collective security will be established with the participation of regional states, and the global economy will improve. And if it does not leave, we will expel it.”Akraminia blamed Washington for the insecurity east of the strait and urged shipowners to use a shipping corridor designated by Iran's armed forces. He claimed vessels travelling along the route would be safe.Meanwhile, Iran's regular navy said it had “monitored” a fire aboard a “violating tanker” in the Gulf of Oman. The navy alleged that the vessel had switched off its tracking systems and attempted to enter a “prohibited zone”.The IRGC navy has warned commercial vessels away from dangerous areas while also advising local fishermen to exercise caution around containers drifting in the water.Houthis advance in YemenElsewhere in the region, fighting intensified around another critical shipping route near the Arabian Peninsula.In Yemen, the Houthis tightened their siege of Taiz, the country's third-largest city, while advancing on several fronts.At the same time, the Saudi-led coalition reported intercepting ballistic missiles and drones targeting Riyadh and other parts of the kingdom.Coalition spokesman Maj Gen Turki al-Maliki said its forces had shot down a ballistic missile heading towards Yanbu, a Red Sea port. articles.title: A blind UK man applied for more than 1,000 jobs without success and spent 16 months unemployed, then built an accessibility business; at 23, Brandon Hulcoop has won the King’s Trust Young Achiever award
articles.summary: For 16 months, Brandon Hulcoop faced rejection after rejection while trying to find work.
articles.body: For 16 months, Brandon Hulcoop faced rejection after rejection while trying to find work. Blind since birth, the 23-year-old had applied for more than 1,000 jobs without securing a position. Instead of allowing that experience to define his prospects, he turned his frustration into a business aimed at making everyday experiences more accessible for people with sight loss. Scroll down to read his story of struggle, inclusion and independence.From job rejections to entrepreneurshipAccording to an AOL report, Hulcoop's turning point came after he received support from The King’s Trust through its Enterprise programme. The experience helped him develop the confidence and practical skills to pursue an idea of his own, eventually leading to the creation of All Things Dotty.The business focuses on accessible products for visually impaired people, their families and organisations, explains the online report. Its range includes Braille menus, greetings cards, board games, card games, colouring books and artwork, bringing accessibility into areas of everyday life that can often be overlooked.Making accessibility more practicalAs per a report by Daily Mail, Hulcoop has taken his work beyond selling accessible products. He also established the UK Sight Loss Collective, which works as a liaison between government and public bodies on issues affecting people with sight loss. His efforts extend into education and community support as well. He offers free Braille tuition to people on low incomes, mentors young people as they enter the workforce and speaks at schools about his experiences. He also serves as an ambassador for sight loss charity Devon in Sight.The combination of entrepreneurship and advocacy has made his work particularly personal. Rather than simply identifying gaps in accessibility, Hulcoop has built practical solutions while helping others navigate some of the barriers he encountered himself.A major recognitionAccording to the AOL report, his determination has now earned Hulcoop The King’s Trust Young Achiever Award at the Pride of Britain Awards. The honour recognises young people who have overcome significant challenges with support from The King’s Trust and gone on to make a difference in the lives of others. The report also mentions that Hulcoop met King Charles at a King’s Trust event in London earlier this month, shortly after learning that he had won the award. articles.title: Cars torched, shops looted: Violence protests erupt across France; over 270 arrested
articles.summary: More than 270 people were arrested across France on Saturday as protests over rising living costs turned violent.
articles.body: More than 270 people were arrested across France on Saturday as protests over rising living costs turned violent. Cars were set ablaze, shops looted, and police used tear gas and water cannons to disperse crowds. Videos from Paris showed protesters climbing a statue to unfurl an anti-police banner, burnt-out vehicles near a major protest square and officers charging demonstrators with batons as the “yellow vest” movement returned to the streets.France's interior ministry reported “a growing number of violent incidents” across the country, including assaults on police officers, looting and damage to public buildings. Several people were injured in clashes.Protesters scale statue as cars burn in ParisA video from Place de la République showed protesters climbing the enormous statue at the centre of the square and unfurling a banner accusing police of injuring high school students. The square is one of France's most famous protest sites and has hosted demonstrations for generations.Another video showed cars completely burnt out on a side street near Place de la République. According to reports by The Associated Press, thick black smoke rose from torched cars, bicycles and other vehicles, while rubbish bins and a kiosk were on fire. Several shops were also looted.Footage from the Opéra district showed police charging a procession of several hundred people with batons and tear gas to break it up. At Place de la République, officers used tear gas and water cannons against masked and hooded protesters throwing fireworks, paving stones and other objects.A separate video from Place de la République purportedly showed a man attacking firefighters twice before a crowd assaulted him.Police also tried to prevent smaller groups from converging on government buildings. Several metro stations were closed at police request, including those near the Champs-Elysées, the presidential palace, parliament and government offices.However, according to the reports by AP, despite the clashes, most demonstrators remained peaceful. A march towards north-western Paris saw crowds chanting France's national anthem and waving flags, while some protesters played trumpets and violins.Fires and damage reported in Lyon, MarseilleThe unrest spread beyond the capital, with fires and damage reported in several major cities.In Lyon, France's third-largest city, a fire broke out inside a tourist office as around 20,000 people joined the march. Smoke and flames were seen rising from the building.In the southern port city of Marseille, shops and a municipal police station were damaged. Protesters also briefly forced their way into the lobby of City Hall.“This is unacceptable," Marseille Mayor Benoît Payan told BFM TV, describing the damage inside City Hall as “limited.”The Interior Ministry also reported violence involving masked groups in Rennes, Toulouse, Montpellier and Grenoble, among other cities.Yellow vests return amid anger over rising pricesThe demonstrations followed calls on social media to revive France's “yellow vest” movement, which emerged in 2018 against social injustice. Many protesters wore the fluorescent yellow vests that became a symbol of those rallies.Demonstrators expressed anger over rising living costs, with gasoline, energy and food prices having spiked in recent months. They also criticised the government over what they described as the neglect of public services and policies favouring the wealthy.Sonia Mabrouk, 40, travelled from a suburb west of Paris with her high school student daughter to protest against “everything that’s going wrong”.Mabrouk, who took part in the original yellow vest protests, criticised “policies that favor the rich and always hit the poorest people in their wallets.”“There’s a general sense of frustration and anger,” she said as she marched alongside peaceful demonstrators of different ages.Unions back protests as student unrest continuesThe latest demonstrations follow weeks of school blockades organised by student groups since mid-September. The groups urged supporters to join the nationwide protests.The CGT, one of France's major labour unions, also backed the rallies, calling for “higher wages and pensions, lower prices and the protection of public services that meet people’s needs.” The union said more than 500,000 people took part in demonstrations across France on Saturday.Far-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon, who has backed the student movement, also joined the Paris protest.The unrest comes after weeks of student-led demonstrations that have resulted in thousands of arrests, hundreds of injuries and schools being set on fire. The protests have also become an issue in France's presidential election campaign and attracted international attention.Some teenagers have suffered serious injuries from police riot-control weapons, according to protesters. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez suspended the use of a type of police stun grenade against young demonstrators after a 15-year-old lost a hand.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Why are Latin American countries building closer ties with Israel?
articles.summary: A wave of new Latin American leaders reverses measures meant to isolate Israel after its genocidal war on Gaza.
articles.body:
When Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar announced on October 8 that Colombia would be moving its embassy to Jerusalem, he made sure to point out how important the development was for his country’s diplomatic narrative, and that it heralded warming relations with Latin American governments.

“We will work hard because this is the diplomatic battle over the truth,” Saar said. “And the truth is, Jerusalem was always the capital of one nation.”

Brazil, Saar went on to say, might soon join Colombia and the growing list of Latin American countries that had moved their embassies to Jerusalem, the disputed city claimed by Israelis and Palestinians as their capital.

Latin America’s relationship with Israel is shifting, as right-wing parties come into power in the region and pro-Israel politicians use their support for the country to rally voters.

Brazil, the largest country in the region, is in the midst of a presidential election campaign in which the relationship with Israel has become a key talking point.

President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, a left-wing ardent supporter of Palestine, is locked in a close contest with right-wing rival Senator Flavio Bolsonaro. He has sported Israeli flags at campaign rallies and played up his friendship with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The pair are scheduled to take part in a run-off election after Bolsonaro performed surprisingly strongly in the first -round, apparently raising hopes for a detente with Israeli officials like the foreign minister.

Last month, for instance, Colombia and Israel began allowing their citizens to travel visa-free between their countries, yet another signal the newly inaugurated government of Abelardo de la Espriella wants to restore ties that were cut in the wake of Israel’s war on Gaza.

Experts say the realignment with Israel is driven, in part, by new leaders trying to signal they have joined a regional alignment with United States President Donald Trump. But it’s also being fuelled by a massive lobbying effort in which Evangelical Christian groups and Israeli-government-backed organisations in the region have pushed Latin American countries to support Israel.

“It’s not one factor or the other, but a convergence,” said Marta Tawil Kuri, Research Professor at the Center for International Studies at the College of Mexico. “Right-wing leaderships seeking validation from Washington, evangelical bases giving them electoral and ideological grounding, and an Israeli diplomatic offensive that finds fertile ground in Latin America precisely as its image deteriorates elsewhere.”

“The most Zionist president in the world”

His successor, de la Espriella, has rapidly reversed Bogota’s stance on Israel since coming to power in August, announcing plans to move his country’s embassy from Tel Aviv to Jerusalem, re-appoint ambassadors and even recognising Israeli control over the occupied Syrian territory of the Golan Heights.

Strong presidential systems and weak, unprofessional diplomatic corps allow new heads of state to quickly pivot on issues such as ties with Israel, said Kuri.

“Unlike the US, where support for Israel has stayed relatively stable across administrations thanks to more consolidated institutions and bipartisan consensus, in much of Latin America foreign policy can swing sharply from one election to the next because that institutional buffer doesn’t exist,” Kuri said.

In 2023, Argentina elected right-wing populist Javier Milei as president, who pledged to move the embassy to Jerusalem, refused to recognise a Palestinian state at the UN and said he was “proud to be the most Zionist president in the world.”

In Bolivia, the leftist administration of Evo Morales, who was president from 2006 to 2019, had refused to have full diplomatic ties with Israel. This continued under the presidency of Luis Arce, who joined other regional left-wing leaders in recalling their ambassadors from Israel after October 7, 2023. When Arce was voted out last year, his replacement Rodrigo Paz promptly reversed that policy.

Soon after coming to office this August, Chilean President Jose Antonio Kast undid his leftist predecessor’s actions against Israel as well, appointing an ambassador to Israel who describes himself as a “proud Zionist”.

Over in Honduras, the left-wing government was replaced by a right-wing leader this January. New President Nasry Asfura, the grandson of Palestinian immigrants from Bethlehem, similarly reappointed an ambassador to Israel this year.

In August, Venezuela announced it would restore consular relations with Israel, undoing nearly two decades of an antagonistic stance towards Israel under previous leaders Nicolas Maduro and Hugo Chavez.

Besides deciding where to put their embassies, Latin American governments have also sometimes lent support to legal efforts against Israel over the Gaza war. Mexico, Bolivia, Colombia, Brazil, Chile, Belize, Cuba and Nicaragua are among governments that at one point backed South Africa’s genocide case against Israel at the International Court of Justice.

When Flavio Bolsonaro launched his Brazilian presidential campaign last July, he did so standing beside Argentinian President Milei. Some in the crowd waved Israeli flags and watched as Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu delivered a video message calling Bolsonaro a friend and a “great champion of the friendship between our peoples”.

Giving foreign leaders such a prominent role in an election campaign is “unheard of in Latin America,” said Alexander Main, Director of International Policy at the Washington-DC-based Center for Economic and Policy Research. “This did not happen before, at least not so overtly.”

Bolsonaro’s campaign, experts say, is seeking to make itself part of a larger political camp that is led in the hemisphere by Trump and internationally includes Israel. Some received direct endorsements from Trump, such as Colombia’s de la Espriella and Honduras’s Asfura.

They’ve joined new right-wing umbrella groups led by the US, such as the Shield of the Americas , a counter-narcotics security alliance bringing together Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, the Dominican Republic, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guyana, Honduras, Panama, Paraguay, Peru and Trinidad and Tobago. The effort is part of Trump’s policy for the Western Hemisphere that seeks to keep out the influence of other global powers like China.

Members of this Trump-led bloc have helped facilitate controversial US policies to deter migration, such as El Salvador, which is housing third-country deportees for the US. They’ve also chosen to frame their war on narcotics as a new kind of war on terrorism, a zero-sum conflict that is inspired by Israel’s war on the Palestinians, according to Main.

“They find common ground with Israel on a lot of these things,” Main said.

“Before, you had left-wing politicians in these regions that have seen what has happened in Gaza and called that war crimes and human rights abuses,” Main said. “Now you’ve seen, on the other hand, sectors seeing this as an existential fight against a deep-rooted enemy and that merits a kind of war on terror framing.”

Having good relations with Israel could translate into access to key military and security resources as well, Main said, including the use of sophisticated spy software such as Pegasus – which was developed by an Israeli software company – and sales of military jets or training of forces.

The rally in August in Brazil that featured Netanyahu’s video message was also an attempt to win support from a large and influential voter bloc there who see protecting Israel as part of their religious worldview.

The Evangelical Parliamentary Front, a caucus of pro-Israel evangelical legislators, includes more than 40% of the Chamber of Deputies and more than a quarter of the Senate. If they formed a party, the loose alliance would become the third-largest in the country.

“Those constituencies have become increasingly politicised in recent years, to the point it is beneficial for politicians to court them and one of the ways they can do that is rallying behind Israel,” Main said.

Brazil is not the only country seeing this evangelical push to build ties with Israel.

“Evangelicalism — particularly Christian Zionism — is a real and growing factor in countries like Honduras and Guatemala,” Kuri said.

Around 40 percent of the population in those countries are evangelicals and both governments have moved their embassies to Jerusalem.

Groups from the US have also been lobbying on Israel’s behalf.

The Latino Coalition for Israel, led by Florida-based evangelical pastor Mario Bramnick, sends delegations throughout Latin America and has met with leaders in Guatemala, El Salvador, Brazil, Panama, Chile, and Costa Rica.

“Our support for Israel is first and foremost rooted in the Bible, where it was clearly established that God gave the Land of Israel, with Jerusalem as its undivided capital, to the Jewish people as an eternal covenant,” the group says on its website. A spokesperson for Bramnick declined to comment for this story.

In 2025, the Genesis Prize – an Israeli nonprofit launched with a $100 million endowment and Israeli government backing – awarded $1m to Argentinian President Milei for his “unequivocal support of Israel during one of the most difficult times since the founding of the Jewish State”.

Milei took the money and established the Isaac Accords, modelling the effort after the Abraham Accords, a Trump-backed effort to restore diplomatic and economic ties between Israel and the Arab world. The initiative gives grant money for pro-Israel civil society groups in Latin America. It also keeps meticulous track of many of the signalling moves right-wing governments are making in recent months to show their new stance on Israel, from moving embassies to Jerusalem to how they vote on Israel-related resolutions in the United Nations.

The initiative’s latest push? At the end of Netanyahu’s trip to the UN General Assembly in late September – where most of the audience walked out of his speech in protest – he and the leaders of Bolivia, Panama and Paraguay held their own summit. The Israeli leader urged them to join the Isaac Accords, writing on X that he sought to “expand the circle of friendship and partnership with Israel”.

articles.summary: An Australia-bound Qantas flight was cancelled after a bedbug infestation was reported on the aircraft, prompting the airline to carry out a deep cleaning
articles.body: An Australia-bound Qantas flight was cancelled after a bedbug infestation was reported on the aircraft, prompting the airline to carry out a deep cleaning of the cabin before it could return to service.The incident occurred after passengers on a nearly 17-hour Qantas flight from Perth to Rome reported being bitten by bedbugs on October 9, The New York Post reported, citing accounts from passengers and other media reports.The airline subsequently cancelled the Rome-to-Perth service scheduled for October 10 to allow engineers and maintenance teams to thoroughly clean the aircraft.“We sincerely apologise to customers for the cancellation of Saturday’s Rome-to-Perth service, which allowed our engineers and maintenance teams to carry out a deep clean of the aircraft after an issue was identified on a small number of economy seats,” Qantas Airways Limited told Fox News Digital.Bedbugs are small insects that feed on human blood and can travel by attaching themselves to luggage, clothing and other personal belongings.Although bedbug bites can cause itching and swelling, the insects are not known to spread disease and are generally not considered a public health hazard.However, travellers can unknowingly carry bedbugs from aircraft to hotels and eventually into their homes.Passenger Hailey Bagnall told Australian broadcaster 9News Sydney that the insects were crawling over passengers’ belongings, clothes and blankets, and were even spotted along the windows.Other passengers also described the experience, with one saying they were woken by screaming, while another claimed the bugs “just kept coming”.Travellers reportedly discovered bedbugs inside their shoes and crawling on their clothing as they collected their belongings. According to 9News, passengers had alerted the flight crew to the insects during an earlier Sydney-to-Perth leg of the journey.What did Qantas do after the bedbug reports?Qantas said it took several precautionary measures before the aircraft's subsequent long-haul journey to Rome, including deep cleaning the cabin, removing seat coverings and soft furnishings, and cordoning off affected seats.The airline also said its aircraft are regularly cleaned to a high standard and undergo precautionary disinfectant treatment every 50 days.Passengers affected by the incident were reportedly given antihistamines to ease itching caused by the bites, although the supply eventually ran out, The Sydney Morning Herald reported.Following the cancellation of the return service, Qantas arranged hotel accommodation for affected travellers and rebooked them on alternative flights within 48 hours.You use AI every day. articles.title: Pete Tong and Sonny Fodera announced for Brighton's On The Beach
articles.summary: The first acts are announced for the 2027 edition of On The Beach in Brighton.
articles.body:
Pete Tong's Ibiza Classics show and DJ Sonny Fodera are the first acts to be announced for Brighton's On The Beach festival in 2027.

Organisers said Pete Tong, with Tom Richards conducting the Essential Orchestra, would perform at the season opening party on 9 July, while Sonny Fodera would take to the stage on 24 July.

The festival returns to Brighton beach for its seventh edition after hosting artists including Fatboy Slim, Madness, The Maccabees and Moby this year .

Festival organisers said the event generated more than £8.3m for Brighton's economy in 2025, attracting about 59,000 attendees and supporting more than 300 jobs.

They said the event delivered more than £3m in visitor spending across local businesses, accommodation and hospitality.

Councillor David McGregor said Brighton council was delighted that On the Beach would return next year.

He said: "Events are critical to making Brighton and Hove such a distinctive place to live, work and visit, and bring significant benefits to our communities and economy."

McGregor added that last year's event created a "second-to-none experience for visitors and residents alike".

A spokesperson for On the Beach said the Pete Tong and Sonny Fodera shows were "a first taste of what's to come" more would be announced in due course.

articles.title: Kolkata Durga Puja Stampede: 17 feared dead; PM Modi, Amit Shah, Mamata express grief
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: At least 17 people were feared dead and 15 injured after a stampede-like incident at a Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata on Saturday evening,
articles.body: NEW DELHI: At least 17 people were feared dead and 15 injured after a stampede-like incident at a Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata on Saturday evening, as heavy rain and a sudden rush of visitors triggered chaos near the exit gate. Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah and former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee expressed grief over the incident.The incident took place at around 7:40 pm at the Sarada Park (Chorbagan) Durga Puja pandal, where a surge of visitors near the exit gate reportedly triggered panic as rain continued to fall.Kolkata Police said all the injured had been rescued and taken to the hospital. Reinforcements, fire brigade personnel, disaster management teams, ambulances and medical staff were sent to the spot. The pandal was subsequently closed to visitors.Prime Minister Narendra Modi said he was deeply distressed by the incident. In a post on X, the Prime Minister’s Office said: “The stampede in Kolkata is extremely distressing. My thoughts are with those who have lost their loved ones. May the injured recover at the earliest. The local administration is providing all possible assistance to those affected.”The PMO also wrote, "The Prime Minister has announced that each relative of those who lost their lives in the stampede in Kolkata will be provided with a one-time financial assistance of 2 lakh rupees from the Prime Minister's National Relief Fund (PMNRF). Each of the injured will be given financial assistance of 50,000 rupees.The Prime Minister has announced that each relative of those who lost their lives in the stampede in Kolkata will be provided with a one-time financial assistance of 2 lakh rupees from the Prime Minister's National Relief Fund (PMNRF). Each of the injured will be given financial assistance of 50,000 rupees."President Droupadi Murmu also expressed sorrow over the reported deaths, describing the incident as “extremely heartbreaking”. She extended her condolences to the bereaved families and prayed for the speedy recovery of those injured.Union home minister Amit Shah also expressed anguish over the incident and said he had spoken with West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari.HM Shah wrote in a post on X, “I pray for the peace of the souls of those who have lost their lives in this tragic accident and extend my deepest condolences to the bereaved family members. The administration is making arrangements for the best possible medical treatment for the injured".Shah also said he would cancel all his scheduled programmes in West Bengal on Sunday to visit the injured in hospital.Mamata All India Trinamool Congress (MAITC) supremo Mamata Banerjee said, “Deeply shocked and saddened to learn about the stampede at the Chore Bagan Puja Pandal. I pray to Maa Durga for the speedy recovery of all those injured and for strength and courage for their families during this difficult time.”Meanwhile, Governor RN Ravi also expressed his grief in a statement issued by Lok Bhavan. “I am deeply heartbroken by the tragic stampede incident at a Durga Puja pandal in Kolkata, resulting in the loss of many precious lives. In this hour of grief, I extend my heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families. I pray for the swift recovery of the injured.”Chief minister Suvendu Adhikari and chief secretary Manoj Agarwal visited the hospital, while health minister Saradwat Mukherjee and other senior officials also reached the hospital to check on the injured.West Bengal minister Nisith Pramanik wrote, "Deeply saddened by the pandal collapse in Chorbagan. My thoughts are with those injured and their families during this difficult time. Our government is working tirelessly to ensure prompt medical care, immediate relief and every possible support for those affected. We stand firmly beside every affected family. Praying for the speedy recovery of all those injured."Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Netanyahu praises Trump's 'wicked sense of humor,' defends ironclad alliance ahead of historic Israel vote
articles.summary: Benjamin Netanyahu praised Donald Trump's "wicked sense of humor" and warmth in a rare look at their bond ahead of Israel's Oct. 27 election.
articles.body: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu offered a rare glimpse into his relationship with President Donald Trump, praising the president's "wicked sense of humor" and their shared commitment to protecting their nations from common threats. Speaking on "Life, Liberty & Levin," the Israeli leader told host Mark Levin that his relationship with Trump is built on years of mutual understanding and shared security concerns. Netanyahu said their partnership could continue to "bring security" if he wins Israel's upcoming election. "I always recognize he's the president of the United States, he does what he thinks is good for the United States. And that's exactly what he does. I do the same for Israel," Netanyahu said. "And I'm glad that it often, very often, this meshes." TRUMP WELCOMES NETANYAHU TO WHITE HOUSE AS RAGING IRAN WAR THREATENS TO SOUR US-ISRAEL RELATIONSHIP Netanyahu also highlighted Trump's personal warmth, a side of the president he said many people may not know about. "Our rapport not only comes from knowing each other for so many years, it's also from understanding that we face a common danger and that we have to protect our common future. And that's really it," Netanyahu said. "Aside from the fact it's fun being with him, I mean, I don't know. Most people don't know that he has a wicked sense of humor. I mean, he can be very funny and very warm. And so, I treasure this relationship," he added. 'BIBI'S HAIR ON FIRE': TRUMP-NETANYAHU PUBLIC 'RIFT' MASKED UNIFIED FRONT AGAINST IRAN, ANALYST SAYS Israel is preparing to hold its first national election since the Oct. 7, 2023, terror attacks and the wars that followed, with voters set to head to the polls Oct. 27. When asked about his political future, Netanyahu said he's focused on winning re-election. "First, I have to get elected," Netanyahu said. "And by the way, I fight every campaign as though I'm [going to] lose, and that's the only reason I win. But I have to fight it in the coming week, and I will." "But God willing, if I'm elected, then this partnership will continue to bring security and bring peace," he added. 'PEACE THROUGH STRENGTH': TRUMP GAZA PLAN GAINS GLOBAL BACKING ONE YEAR ON NETANYAHU REJECTS REPORTS OF A RIFT WITH PRESIDENT TRUMP, SAYS THE TWO REMAIN ALIGNED ON IRAN Netanyahu is Israel's longest-serving prime minister and has worked closely with Trump during both of Trump's presidential terms. While their relationship remains close, it has not been without friction. Earlier this year, Trump confirmed reports of a heated phone call during which he called Netanyahu "f---ing crazy" over Israel's military operations in Lebanon. Trump also emphasized that he "really love[s] Bibi" and works with him "excellently." Netanyahu later described the disagreement on CNBC as "tactical disagreements" that happen "in the best of families." articles.title: Three men get 158 years each for murdering American and Australian surfers, dumping bodies in Mexican well
articles.summary: Three men were sentenced to 158 years each in Ensenada, Baja California, for the murders of surfers Callum and Jake Robinson and Carter Redd Rhoad.
articles.body: Three men in Mexico received 158-year prison sentences Friday for the murders of Australian surfers Callum and Jake Robinson and their American friend Carter Redd Rhoad. A federal judge in the town of Ensenada, Baja California sentenced Jesús Gerardo García, Irineo Francisco and Ángel Jesús each to 158 years and nine months in prison for murder, robbery with violence and vehicle theft with violence. An accomplice of García's — Ary Gisell Silva Raya — was also convicted of aggravated robbery with violence and vehicle theft with violence and sentenced to 20 years in November after agreeing to an abbreviated trial. AMERICANS WARNED POPULAR TRAVEL ROUTES THIS SUMMER COULD CARRY CRIME AND KIDNAPPING RISKS García, Francisco and Jesús were convicted last week of killing the Robinson brothers and Rhoad, which authorities said was carried out in order to steal the tires from the deceased men's truck. "The attackers pull out a gun they were carrying and kill the person who initially resisted the robbery, then on the other two," Baja California prosecutor María Elena Andrade said, according to a report from The Associated Press. THREE WOMEN FOUND DEAD IN POPULAR AMERICAN TOURIST HOT SPOT AS LOCAL POLICE SEARCH FOR CLUES Mexican authorities found the trio's bodies in a well in the state of Baja California in May 2024. The three men traveled to Punta San José, about 50 miles from where their bodies were found in Ensenada, for a surfing trip in April 2024. MEXICAN SPORTS JOURNALIST ROBBED AT GUNPOINT DURING LIVE REPORT The parents of the Robinsons attended the sentencing, telling reporters the moment marked a significant conclusion to the tragic two years since their sons' deaths. "Today’s guilty verdict is a significant moment in our long and painful journey to seek justice for our beautiful sons, Callum and Jake, and their friend Carter Rhoad, whose lives were so cruelly taken from them in 2024," Matin Robinson said. POPULAR CRUISE LINE'S GIANT BEACH PARK BLOCKED BY MEXICO AFTER LOCAL BACKLASH ERUPTS The deaths captured international attention and rocked the local economy, which authorities said was heavily reliant on tourism. Antonio Otañez, president of the Baja California surfers association, said he was happy to see justice served but admitted the incident led to a "major drop" in tourism. articles.title: 'He kept on hitting': Indian flydubai pilot Smit Machchhar reveals what happened mid-flight as he was stabbed
articles.summary: Indian pilot Smit Machchhar who was attacked by his co-pilot aboard a Flydubai flight has recalled how a routine journey turned into a fight for survival,
articles.body: Indian pilot Smit Machchhar who was attacked by his co-pilot aboard a Flydubai flight has recalled how a routine journey turned into a fight for survival, describing the repeated blows to his head, his attempts to call for help and the moments he lost consciousness as the aircraft went into a dive.after he was stabbed by his Omani copilot Hamam Al Hammami who was allegedly trying to crash the plane.In an exclusive 1st news interview after being stabbed, with Sky News Arabia, Captain Smith Machchhar said there had been nothing unusual about the flight until about two hours after take-off. He was carrying out routine checks in the cockpit when the attack began, initially mistaking the first blow to the back of his head for damage to the aircraft.Giving out details as he remembered he said, "when I was just in in the checking my computer for the timing and everything, uh suddenly there was a a very hard hit at the back of my head, right here. And uh it was quite hard and felt that it was something which was very strong."He said he initially thought something had broken off the aircraft's roof and hit him, causing catastrophic damage. Drawing on his training, he tried to regain his composure and check the aircraft's systems. “My thought process went on that track, that oh, there is a big damage in the aircraft which has hit me at the back,” he said.But within seconds, he realised he was being attacked. “He kept on hitting,” Machchhar said. He recalled turning around and realising what was happening, although the impact had severely restricted his field of vision.“Immediately, I would say in the next few seconds, my vision was restricted to like few inches,” he said, adding that he learnt about the extent of the impact from doctors later.His first response was to protect himself from further blows. He quickly unbuckled his seatbelt, turned around and tried to block the attack, sustaining an injury to his hand. “At this point, it was very obvious what was going on,” he said.‘Smith, do something. You can’t die like this’Machchhar said he immediately tried to get help from another captain who was on board and was expected to operate the return flight. “I was screaming his name and I was trying because the switch was very close to me to open the door. I was trying to just get help in,” he said.He lost consciousness amid the commotion but remembered managing to open the cockpit door. He could hear shouting as the other crew members confronted the co-pilot. “The door shut immediately after that because he threatened to hit them as well,” Machchhar said.By then, he was struggling to stay conscious and could feel his strength fading because of blood loss. Soon afterwards, he heard the engine sounds change and felt the aircraft go into a dive. “Since I’ve been flying for such a long time, I don’t have to see the instruments to figure out or hear the engine to know what’s happening,” he said.Machchhar said he repeatedly drifted in and out of consciousness but realised he had to fight to survive. “There was a moment where I realised and I told myself that, ‘Smith, do something. You can’t die like this,’” he said.His memories of what happened next remain fragmented. He recalled trying to reach the door, bracing his leg against something and pushing himself forward.“The next memory that I have is the door’s open and I’m lying between the cockpit and the galley,” he said. He remembered being face down as panic and shouting continued around him.‘Everyone did their best’While Machchhar was fighting to survive, another captain took over the controls and helped save the aircraft. “The other thing, how my other colleague who took over the controls and saved the day again is commendable. It’s something that I’ll keep with me till I die,” he said.Asked what he wanted people to understand about the incident amid speculation over how the plane was saved, Machchhar said everyone on board had done what they could.“I think everyone in world everyone in world did the best in their capacity to save the day,” he said. The pilot said the first blow continued to haunt him in the days after the attack.“Immediately after the event, I used to get flashes of the first hit. And trust me, it shook me up for the first few days,” he said, describing how the memory would return suddenly and leave his heart racing.But what stayed with him most was the determination of those on board. “One thing that I would take away from that day was the determination, the sheer determination of everyone to survive,” he said.Machchhar said he felt out of danger only when the aircraft touched down in Saudi Arabia. By then, a doctor was attending to him in the galley, while crew members worked to keep him conscious.Asked whom he thought of first, he replied: “My son.” His two-year-old son, wife and daughter live with him in the UAE.Machchhar also expressed gratitude for the medical treatment he received in Saudi Arabia and after being brought back to the UAE. “From the first day onwards, the way I was taken care of, the way I was brought back to the UAE, even the care that I was given in Saudi is something I would never forget in my life,” he said.Still recovering from the traumatic incident, he said he felt grateful for the care and support he had received over the preceding two-and-a-half weeks.“Grateful is the word I would say right now,” he said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Saudi Arabia executes five nationals on terrorism charges, death toll hits 188
articles.summary: Saudi Arabia executed five of its nationals on terrorism charges in the Eastern Province on Saturday, October 17, after their convictions were upheld and
articles.body: Saudi Arabia executed five of its nationals on terrorism charges in the Eastern Province on Saturday, October 17, after their convictions were upheld and royal orders were issued for the sentences to be carried out, the kingdom's Ministry of Interior said. The executions bring the total number of people put to death in Saudi Arabia this year to 188, according to an AFP tally based on official statements.The five men were convicted of joining a foreign terrorist organisation, opening fire on security forces and providing support for terrorist operations inside the kingdom.In its statement, the Ministry of Interior cited Quranic verses condemning corruption and violence. It said the men had been convicted of crimes involving attacks on security personnel, the use of weapons and the provision of support and safe houses to finance and carry out terrorist operations in Saudi Arabia.The ministry said the men were identified as Mohammed bin Munir bin Mohammed Al-Zaher, Ali bin Abdulrab Al-Hussein Al-Sheikh, Hassan bin Zaki bin Mohammed Al-Faraj, Rida bin Mohammed bin Ali Al Abdullah and Ali bin Hassan bin Ahmed Al Rih.According to the statement, security authorities arrested the men and completed investigations before referring them to the competent court. The court sentenced them to death after finding them guilty of the charges. The sentences were upheld by the Supreme Court, and royal orders were issued for their implementation.The executions took place in the Eastern Province, which is home to most of Saudi Arabia's Shia Muslim minority. The community has long complained of marginalisation in the Sunni-majority kingdom.Ministry warns against attacks on securityIn its statement, the ministry said the executions demonstrated the government's commitment to maintaining security and enforcing Islamic law. It warned that anyone who attacks the security of others or violates their right to life and safety would face the consequences under the law.The ministry also invoked Quranic verses prohibiting corruption on earth and those prescribing punishment for people who wage war against God and his messenger and spread disorder.Saudi Arabia's execution toll risesSaudi Arabia has executed 15 people on terrorism convictions since January, most of them in the Eastern Province, compared with 40 such executions in 2025, according to AFP.The latest executions come as the kingdom faces missile and drone attacks by Yemen's Houthi rebels. Riyadh backs Yemen's internationally recognised government in the country's long-running civil war against the Iran-backed group.Saudi Arabia was the world's third-most prolific executioner between 2022 and 2025, behind China and Iran, according to Amnesty International.The kingdom maintains that capital punishment is necessary to preserve public order and says death sentences are carried out only after all appeals have been exhausted.You use AI every day. articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Friday said the US was working to set up a trilateral meeting with Russia as a platform to discuss peace
articles.body: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Friday said the US was working to set up a trilateral meeting with Russia as a platform to discuss peace negotiations, stating Kyiv was ready to hold meetings anywhere, in any format.Zelenskyy laid out several possible venues for the trilateral discussion, including during G20 summit in the US.“Another possibility is for the meeting to take place in the United States during the G20 summit. But there has been no confirmation yet from Russia or from the United States,” Zelenskyy said in a post on X.He said the meeting could also take place in Saudi Arabia, the UAE or European countries.Zelenskyy also expressed his disappointment with recent US-Russia engagement and energy deal, stressing that the pressure needs to be on Moscow, not Kyiv.“We’re counting on them to put more pressure on Putin, not on us,” Zelenskyy said.“Otherwise, it’s simply unfair,” he added.The Ukrainian President said Europeans need to have their own infrastructure and their own track for negotiations with Russia, and not overly rely on the United States.We need to pursue every possible avenue to stop the war, he said.Land beyond negotiationsRussia, however, has hinted that some of Ukraine’s territories may exist beyond peace talksRussian President Vladimir Putin said on Friday that Moscow was establishing a buffer “security zone” inside Ukraine to protect Russia’s border regions, adding that the zone would not be part of any future peace negotiations.Putin made the remarks during a visit to a command post of Russia’s joint military task force. He linked the operation to Ukraine’s incursion into Russia’s western Kursk region in 2024-25, saying Russian forces had been instructed to drive Ukrainian troops out of Russian territory and extend the operation into neighbouring Ukrainian territory.“The Russian armed forces were tasked not only with expelling the enemy from our land but also with establishing a security zone in the adjacent territory. Its principal members and partners include Iran, Hezbollah in Lebanon, the Houthis in Yemen, Hamas and Palestinian Islamic Jihad in the Palestinian territories, among others.The explosion occurred amid heightened regional instability, including continued tensions surrounding the Strait of Hormuz and escalating clashes between the Saudi-led coalition and Yemen’s Houthis.On Friday, the US claimed that Tehran was facing severe financial pressure and was unable to fund its allied armed groups because of a naval blockade imposed by Washington. articles.title: Deva’s humility remained one of his most endearing qualities
articles.summary: Deva’s humility and admiration for fellow composers defined his legacy as a prolific Tamil film music icon, inspiring generations and everyday life moments.
articles.body: Chennai: If his music was uncomplicated, so was the man behind it. Deva’s humility remained one of his most endearing qualities. Success neither distanced him from his roots nor prevented him from appreciating the achievements of fellow composers.Unlike the fiercely competitive image often associated with the film industry, Deva openly admired his contemporaries. He spoke appreciatively of Ilaiyaraaja and A R Rahman and was equally enthusiastic about younger musicians. In an earlier interview, he acknowledged that ego had no place in his musical journey. Even during his busiest years, he would personally contact fellow composers to express his admiration for their work.That absence of professional insecurity was central to his character. He never hesitated to sing under composers much younger than himself. Whether it was Anirudh Ravichander, G V Prakash Kumar, or Santhosh Narayanan, Deva was always willing to lend his distinctive voice and learn from an evolving musical landscape. His outlook reflected a rare quality in an industry where generations often compete for relevance: the willingness to remain a student despite being a master.Even in June 2026, while discussing his work on ‘Charukesi’, Deva expressed the excitement of a newcomer fulfilling a long-cherished ambition to compose music rooted in Carnatic classical traditions. After decades of commercial success, there were still musical territories he wished to explore.There was something particularly touching about that enthusiasm. Here was a composer who had scored for hundreds of films, helped shape the musical identities of superstars, and created songs that far outlived their films, yet continued to approach music with curiosity rather than complacency.Deva’s journey remains a reminder that talent does not always arrive with privilege. From modest beginnings and years of uncertainty to becoming one of Tamil cinema’s most prolific composers, his career was built on patience, adaptability, and an instinctive understanding of audiences.With his son Srikanth Deva following him into film music, the family’s artistic legacy continues. Ultimately, Deva’s impact cannot be measured merely by film counts or chartbusters. articles.body: PUDUCHERRY: Madras high court has directed the Central Information Commission (CIC), New Delhi, to consider and dispose of a second appeal filed under the Right to Information (RTI) Act, 2005, by a teaching faculty member at a govt arts and science college in Puducherry within a period of eight weeks.Justice Hemant Chandangoudar passed the order while disposing of a petition filed by assistant professor and head of the department of botany at Tagore Government Arts and Science College (TAC), Puducherry S Ramakrishnan.He initially filed an RTI application on Feb 20, 2026, seeking information relating to the appointment of the controller of examinations and deputy controllers of examinations in TAC.Dissatisfied with the response provided by the PIO, he filed a first appeal on March 24, 2026, before the First Appellate Authority (principal in-charge) of the college. As the outcome of the first appeal remained unsatisfactory, the professor preferred a second appeal before the CIC on May 23, 2026.Aggrieved by the delay in the disposal of his second appeal by the CIC, he then approached the Madras high court in Sept. During the proceedings, Puducherry govt advocate Ramaswamy Meyyappan assured the court that the second appeal would be disposed of at the earliest in accordance with the law.Recording the submission, the high court disposed of the petition with a specific directive on Oct 1 to the Registrar of the CIC to decide on the second appeal on its own merits and pass appropriate orders within eight weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of the order.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Puducherry | Silver Rate in Puducherry | Bank Holidays in Puducherry | Public Holidays in PuducherryStay updated with the latest Puducherry news. articles.title: India vs West Indies T20I series 2026 report card: Grading every player from both teams
articles.summary: India vs West Indies T20I series 2026 report card: Complete player ratings and letter grades (A+ to F) for every player from Team India and the West Indies.
articles.body:
Shai Hope's two unbeaten centuries and Keemo Paul's five-for make them the West Indies' standout performers.

India skipper Shreyas Iyer tops India's grades, while Sanju Samson and Shivam Dube fall short.

The series ended level at 2-2, after rain washed away the third T20I in Bengaluru.

India vs West Indies 2026 T20I report card: Full player grades, top performers and major concerns

The India versus West Indies series ended at 2-2 after the fifth T20I match in Bengaluru had to be abandoned due to rain.

The two teams have traded blows from the opening game, and neither has managed to hold an advantage for long. India won the first T20I in Lucknow by chasing 172 in only 14.4 overs, with Iyer smashing an unbeaten 102 off 43 balls.

West Indies hit back in Ranchi by reaching a target of 250 in 18.3 overs, thanks to a ferocious 102 not out off 45 balls from Shai Hope and an 84 from Sherfane Rutherford. India then won a high-scoring contest in Indore by 14 runs, and West Indies levelled the series in Hyderabad with a 24-run victory after posting 247 for 3.

* Only the performances in the first four T20Is have been taken into consideration.

India won by 8 wickets (172/2 in 14.4 overs)

West Indies won by 6 wickets (252/4 in 18.3 overs)

West Indies won by 24 runs (247/3 vs 223)

Shreyas Iyer (captain): A- Iyer finished as India's leading run-scorer with 159 runs in four innings at a strike rate of about 215, and his unbeaten 102 off 43 balls in Lucknow was the best innings by an Indian batter in the series. He added a quick 40 off 18 balls in Ranchi, which lifted India to 249, although that total still proved too small on the night. Scores of 1 and 16 in Indore and Hyderabad were a letdown, and his captaincy was tested when the West Indies batters scored heavily. Those two low scores are the only thing keeping him from the top grade.

Abhishek Sharma: B+ Abhishek gave India fast starts in most of the games, scoring 139 runs off 76 balls at a strike rate of about 183. His 69 off 30 balls in Indore, which included five sixes and a fifty in just 18 balls, was the best of his four knocks and laid the foundation for a total of 223. He made 21 and 20 in the first two matches at better than a run a ball, but he fell to Roston Chase both times. However, his 29 off 24 balls in the chase in Hyderabad was too slow for a target of 248, and that lapse stops him from earning a higher mark.

Ishan Kishan: B+ Kishan scored 123 runs off 70 balls at a strike rate of roughly 176 and kept the scoreboard moving in the first three games. He stayed unbeaten on 37 in the Lucknow chase, made 43 off 22 balls in Ranchi and added 37 off 18 in Indore. His final outing was a three-ball 6 in Hyderabad, which came at a time when India needed a solid platform. He also held three catches in the field across the series, which adds a little to his case.

Tilak Varma: A Tilak did not bat in Lucknow because the chase ended early, but he made the most of his three innings after that. He scored 115 runs off 59 balls at a strike rate of about 195, including an unbeaten 44 off 18 balls in Ranchi, 28 in Indore and 43 off 25 in Hyderabad. His 43 was the top score in the Hyderabad chase, and he fell at 200 for 6 with 48 still needed from 18 balls. He also took three catches, one in Lucknow and two in Indore, and he is one of the few Indian players who has been steady throughout.

Sanju Samson (wicketkeeper): B- Samson scored 152 runs off 79 balls at a strike rate above 190, but his innings of 11, 82, 3 and 56 show how uneven his contribution has been. His 82 off 41 balls in Ranchi and 56 off 23 in Hyderabad, with half-centuries reached in 21 and 20 balls respectively, were of match-winning quality. However, he was dismissed cheaply in two of the four games, including a three-ball stay in Indore that left India at 7 for 1. He also took two catches behind the stumps, and the inconsistency remains the main worry about his place at the top.

Naman Dhir: B+ Naman took five wickets in 10 overs, and his three for 31 in Lucknow, which included Shai Hope, Romario Shepherd and Shamar Springer, was the best bowling effort by an Indian in the series. He added two more in Indore, removing Kamil Pooran and Shimron Hetmyer, who had both been scoring freely. His economy of about 11.4 is high, as he went for 19 in a single over in Hyderabad and 25 in two in Ranchi. With the bat he made 14 runs from 7 balls, including a duck in Hyderabad.

Nitish Kumar Reddy: B Nitish played in Indore and Hyderabad and gave India useful balance in both. He scored 62 runs off 34 balls, with 21 in Indore and a quick 41 off 20 in Hyderabad, where he added 50 for the sixth wicket with Tilak Varma. With the ball he picked up the wicket of Quentin Sampson in Indore and finished with one wicket from five overs at an economy of 11.6. It is a small sample, although both of his performances were positive.

Axar Patel: C+ Axar took four wickets, two for 26 in Lucknow and one each in Indore and Hyderabad, but he was expensive in the other games and finished with an economy of about 12.2. His 63 runs in 3.3 overs in Ranchi was the costliest spell by any Indian bowler in the series. He also made 20 in Indore before being run out and 3 in Hyderabad. The wickets keep him in the middle ranks, yet his bowling has not given India the control they expect from him.

Shivam Dube: D Dube had only one significant outing, in Ranchi, where he made 7 off 10 balls before being bowled by Chase. He bowled two overs in the same match and gave away 30 runs without taking a wicket. He was in the XI for Lucknow but neither batted nor bowled, and he was not part of the team in the next two games. The sample is small, but the one opportunity he got did not go well.

Arshdeep Singh: B- Arshdeep took five wickets in the four games, including three for 44 in Indore where he dismissed Hope, Rutherford and Keemo Paul. His economy of nearly 11 and 52 runs in Hyderabad took some shine off those numbers, however, and he was injured and retired hurt after scoring 5 with the bat in that game. He also made 11 in Indore. The new-ball wickets were useful, but the death overs remain a problem for him.

Mayank Yadav: B Mayank took four wickets, and his three for 36 in Ranchi was a superb burst because he removed Pooran, Hetmyer for a golden duck and Powell in the powerplay. He was also the most economical Indian seamer in Indore, conceding just 34 runs in four overs with 11 dot balls. However, he leaked 52 runs in Hyderabad and finished with an overall economy of about 10.8. He is a bowler who can change a match in a spell, although he has not yet done it every time.

Prince Yadav: B Prince played in Indore and Hyderabad and bowled eight overs for 73 runs, an economy of about 9.1, which is the best among India's regular seamers. His only wicket was Hetmyer, caught and bowled in Hyderabad after the batter had scored a rapid 33. He also made an unbeaten 13 off 6 balls with three fours in Indore, although he was bowled first ball in Hyderabad. It was a steady performance from a bowler who has been given limited chances.

Kuldeep Yadav: B Kuldeep played only the first two matches and took three wickets for 86 runs from eight overs. His two for 33 in Lucknow, in which he removed Chase and Forde, helped to bring about a West Indies collapse from 114 for 4 to 135 for 8. In Ranchi, he picked up Rutherford but gave away 53 runs. He was not in the team for Indore or Hyderabad, so the sample is small, but the Lucknow spell was good.

Shai Hope (captain, wicketkeeper): A+ Hope scored 261 runs in four innings at a strike rate of roughly 190, and two of them were unbeaten hundreds, 102 off 45 balls in Ranchi and 102 off 50 in Hyderabad. His 52 off 37 balls in Lucknow was a solid start, and only a five-ball 5 in Indore interrupted the run of big scores. He also led the side calmly and made three dismissals behind the stumps, including stumpings of Ishan Kishan and Naman Dhir. No other player in either squad has had such a decisive influence on the series, which is why he earns the only A+.

Sherfane Rutherford: A Rutherford scored 221 runs at a strike rate of about 189 and averaged above 70 for the series. His 84 off 37 balls in Ranchi, which included seven sixes, turned a chase of 250 into a procession, and his 56 off 34 in Lucknow was one of two half-centuries in a losing cause. He added 32 in Indore before finishing unbeaten on 49 off 26 balls in Hyderabad, which pushed West Indies past 240. He is the batter India's bowlers have found hardest to stop after Hope.

Shimron Hetmyer: B+ Hetmyer scored 81 runs off only 41 balls at a strike rate close to 198, although his returns were uneven. He was run out for 5 in Lucknow and bowled first ball by Mayank Yadav in Ranchi, but he came alive in the last two games with 43 off 26 balls in Indore and a rapid 33 off 12 in Hyderabad. His quick runs in Hyderabad took West Indies to 110 for 2 in the eighth over, which set up the big total. The two early failures keep him just below the top bracket.

Kamil Pooran: C+ Pooran made 58 runs in three games at a strike rate of 145 and played only one innings of note, a 42 off 27 balls in Indore. He fell for 12 off 11 balls in Lucknow and for 4 off two balls in Ranchi, so his record was inconsistent. He was not part of the side in Hyderabad, where Jewel Andrew took his place. The strike rate is respectable; however, it is lower than most of the other top-order players.

Rovman Powell: C Powell made 53 runs off 40 balls at a strike rate of about 132, which is modest for a middle-order hitter. His scores were 0, 24, 5 and 24, and on both occasions when he reached 24 he failed to turn the start into a major contribution. He was dismissed by Axar Patel twice in four games. He also bowled 0.2 overs for 7 runs in Ranchi, and he has not been the finisher West Indies hoped for.

Jewel Andrew: C+ Andrew played only in Hyderabad, where he opened with Hope and made 21 off 16 balls. The pair raced to 50 in 22 balls, helped by 11 extras, before he was trapped lbw by Axar Patel at 52. His strike rate of 131 was modest for the situation, but he gave the innings a decent start and also took two catches in the field, those of Kishan and Iyer.

Quentin Sampson: C Sampson featured only in Indore, where he made 21 off 15 balls in the middle order. His innings helped add 46 runs for the fifth wicket and kept West Indies in the chase until the 16th over. He was caught by Tilak Varma off Nitish Kumar Reddy, and with only one innings there is little more to judge him on.

Keemo Paul: A- Paul played only the last two games, but he has made the biggest bowling impact for West Indies. His five for 41 in Hyderabad, which included Samson, Kishan, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Axar Patel and Prince Yadav, turned a chase of 248 into a collapse. He also took one wicket in Indore and made a six-ball 10 with the bat. His six wickets at an economy of just under 10 are very good, although he did send down five wides in Hyderabad.

Roston Chase: A- Chase took six wickets at an economy of about 9.1, the best figures among the regular West Indies bowlers, and his three for 24 in Ranchi was the most economical spell of the series. He dismissed Abhishek in Lucknow, Abhishek, Kishan and Dube in Ranchi, and Kishan and Iyer in Indore, which means he took the wicket of at least one big Indian batter in three of the four games. He went wicketless for 43 runs in Hyderabad. With the bat, he made 5 and an unbeaten 5, so the grade is based almost entirely on his bowling.

Romario Shepherd: B- Shepherd batted twice and bowled in three games, and his best contribution was an unbeaten 34 off 13 balls with three sixes that helped finish the Ranchi chase. He made 7 off 5 balls in Lucknow and took one wicket, Tilak Varma, in Hyderabad. However, he conceded 103 runs in 8.4 overs, an economy of nearly 12, and he missed the Indore match.

Shamar Springer: C+ Springer bowled in all four games and took five wickets, including Samson and Iyer in Ranchi, Abhishek in Indore and Iyer again in Hyderabad. His economy of nearly 13 was high, and he conceded 64 runs in four overs in Ranchi. With the bat, he hit an unbeaten 35 off 11 balls in Indore, which included four sixes and took West Indies close to a total they had no right to chase. He picked up valuable wickets, but the cost has been high.

Matthew Forde: D Forde played only in Lucknow, where he made 2 off 4 balls and was caught by Kishan off Kuldeep Yadav. He then bowled two overs that went for 39 runs without a wicket, an economy of 19.5, as Iyer and Kishan took the chase apart. He was not part of the team for the remaining three games. The sample is very small, but the one outing was poor.

Gudakesh Motie: B+ Motie played from the second match onwards and took three wickets for 71 runs in eight overs, an economy of just under 9. His two for 13 in two overs in Hyderabad removed Abhishek Sharma and Naman Dhir in the space of one ball (the latter stumped by Hope), and it helped to turn the match. He also dismissed Naman in Indore. He was used sparingly in the last game, though the spells he did get were tidy.

Akeal Hosein: C Hosein played the first two matches and took one wicket, a caught-and-bowled of Samson in Lucknow, where he conceded 37 runs in four overs. He was hit hard in Ranchi, going for 46 in three overs without a wicket. He also made 15 off 9 balls in Lucknow, which was a useful lower-order effort. He was not in the side for the last two games.

Shamar Joseph: D+ Joseph took two wickets, both in Indore, where he dismissed Samson for 3 and bowled Mayank Yadav, but he conceded 54 runs in four overs on the day. His economy over the series was above 14, and he gave away 47 in 2.3 overs in Hyderabad. He was also unbeaten on 0 in Lucknow. The pace is there, but the control has been missing, and he has been the most expensive of the West Indies regulars.

India's batters need consistency, and their bowlers need better death-over control

A shortened game of nine overs is a poor way to end a series that was so evenly poised, and the 2-2 result leaves India with more to work on than to celebrate. The home side had reached 118 for 5 in 7.4 overs before the rain ended the match, which was a healthy rate of 15.39 an over, but the way in which those five wickets fell said as much about their weaknesses as the runs said about their power.

Sanju Samson remains the biggest talking point. His scores of 11, 82, 3, 56 and 16 show a batter who can destroy an attack in a matter of overs, yet he has been bowled or dismissed cheaply in three of the five games. He was bowled by Shamar Springer again on Saturday, and the next step for him is to build an innings against the new ball before he begins to attack.

Abhishek Sharma is in a similar position, because his 6 off 4 balls was another early exit, and he has now fallen to Roston Chase twice and to Paul once. His 69 in Indore proved what he can do, although a slow 29 off 24 balls in Hyderabad suggests he is less comfortable when the start has to be measured.

Shreyas Iyer's form after the Lucknow century is the other worry for the management. He scored 1, 16 and 22 in the last three innings, and both he and Tilak Varma, who made only 7 off six balls and was bowled by Springer, were out to deliveries they would normally put away. Ishan Kishan, who hit 30 off 10, and Naman Dhir, who struck an unbeaten 24 off six, were the positives, but both have also had low scores in the series, so their improvement lies in turning cameos into longer stays.

The bowling needs even more work. Axar Patel went for more than 12 an over across the series, Arshdeep Singh was costly at the death before his injury in Hyderabad, and Mayank Yadav conceded 52 in a single game. Shivam Dube has not been seen since Ranchi, and the pace attack as a whole has not yet found a way to contain big hitters in the last five overs.

India have the batting depth to win most T20Is, but unless the top order becomes steadier and the bowlers tighten up, they will keep giving opponents a way back in.

articles.title: Indian diaspora in UK, Ireland protest against SIR
articles.summary: Indian diaspora in London and Dublin protests Special Intensive Revision of India’s electoral rolls, citing voting rights concerns and alleged police action in Delhi.
articles.body: Hyderabad: Members of the Indian diaspora, including those from the Telugu community, staged fresh protests in London and Dublin against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in India, expressing solidarity with protesters in the country and raising concerns over the alleged police action in Delhi.In London, the UK unit of the Students’ Federation of India (SFI) organised demonstrations on Friday outside the Indian High Commission and near the Gandhi statue in Parliament Square. Hundreds of Indians joined the protest, demanding electoral integrity and the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar, according to SFI-UK.Addressing the gathering, SFI-UK president Dr Aparna Vinod said, “We have regressed back in history and we are protesting for our right to vote, the most basic right of any democracy. This right to vote was not given to us. It was won for us. It was fought and won for us by the blood and sweat of freedom fighters and revolutionaries.”SFI-UK alleged that right-wing groups attempted to disrupt the demonstration, but protesters stood their ground and continued raising slogans against what they described as an assault on Indian democracy. The SFI’s Leeds unit staged another protest outside Indian High Commission in London. In Dublin, several members of the Indian diaspora gathered near the Spire for a separate demonstration organised by the South Asia Collective, Ireland.Protesters raised slogans such as “Azadi” and “Inquilab Zindabad”, expressing solidarity with those opposing the SIR in India. articles.title: Cybercrime, terrorism remain key internal security challenges: Home secretary
articles.summary: Home secretary Govind Mohan says cybercrime and terrorism remain key security challenges; govt targets drug-free India in 3 years; urges tougher, forensic-led policing.
articles.body: Hyderabad: The nation will be made drug-free within three years under an action plan unveiled by the Union home ministry, home secretary Govind Mohan said on Saturday, conveying a message from Union home minister Amit Shah at the SVPNPA Dikshant passing-out parade. Reading out Shah’s message to the 78th Regular Recruit (RR) IPS batch, Mohan said tackling drug trafficking required coordinated action against networks, technology-based investigations and greater public awareness.Shah’s message also called for effective implementation of the three new criminal laws, greater use of forensic science and sensitivity in investigations. It reiterated govt’s zero-tolerance approach to terrorism under the Prahar strategy, emphasising time-bound action, better intelligence coordination and a whole-of-govt approach to national security.Mohan said India’s conventional internal security challenges had changed significantly, even as new threats emerged. “Left-wing extremism has conclusively come to an end. Insurgency in the Northeast has reduced to minuscule proportions,” he said, adding that much of the remaining unrest in parts of the Northeast stemmed from ethnic conflicts rather than insurgency. However, he cautioned that terrorism remained a concern. Referring to the recent 2025 Red Fort blast in Delhi, Mohan said homegrown terrorism had not ended completely and foreign-inspired terrorism continued to pose a threat in some parts of the country.Cybercrime was another major challenge, he said, adding that the proliferation of UPI accounts and fake SIM cards had made it easier for people with limited technical skills to commit offences. “Cybercrime has little entry barriers. People with very little skill and knowledge can easily become cybercriminals today,” he said, adding that states and UTs would have to play a central role in tackling the problem.He also flagged illegal immigration, stressing the need to identify illegal foreign nationals and take action against them in accordance with the law. He said the challenges included crime, radicalisation and distortions in markets. “While Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam has been a lifelong and millennia-old adage of this country, the primary charge on this country’s resources is that of the citizens of this country,” he added.The parade marked the completion of 45 weeks of phase I training for 135 IPS probationers. A total of 151 officer trainees participated in the parade, including 16 foreign officer trainees from Bhutan, the Maldives and Nepal. Academy director Sujeet Pandey said, “Our objective has been to prepare future police leaders who are intelligence-led, technology-enabled, evidence-based, and citizen-centric.” The probationers will undergo four weeks of attachment with the Army and central armed police forces before beginning 29 weeks of district practical training from Nov 23. articles.title: 10 fake cops held for abducting jeweller, extorting ₹1.3 cr
articles.summary: Hyderabad police arrest 10 fake cops for abducting a jeweller over a real estate dispute, extorting ₹1.3 crore; two accused still absconding.
articles.body: Hyderabad: A real estate dispute allegedly led to the kidnapping of a jewellery businessman, with a gang posing as police personnel which abducted him and demanded ₹15 crore from his family before releasing him for a ransom of ₹1.3 crore, police said. Ten people have been arrested, while two others remain absconding.K Srinivas Rao (53) went missing on Oct 5 while he was on his way to his jewellery shop in Ramanthapur. Following a complaint by his brother-in-law, Chikkadpally police registered a missing person case and launched an investigation. Rao later told police that he was abducted near Golnaka flyover, blindfolded and held captive at an undisclosed location.Investigators suspect the kidnapping was planned by Dumavath Srikanth, the alleged prime conspirator, over a dispute linked to a real estate venture in Hemanagar, Boduppal. Police said Srikanth allegedly conspired with associates in Aug to abduct Rao, settle the dispute and further extort money from his family.The gang allegedly posed as police personnel during the abduction and used vehicles fitted with fake number plates. They frequently switched vehicles to avoid detection while keeping Rao in captivity.Chikkadpally police, in coordination with the Commissioner’s Task Force, arrested 10 people on Saturday. The arrested include Srikanth and Gunjapogu Suresh alias Surya. Officials seized over ₹1 crore in cash, gold ornaments weighing 118 grams, four cars, two two-wheelers and nine mobile phones.According to the officials, some of the arrested accused had previous criminal cases involving cheating, theft, robbery and kidnapping. Srikanth was allegedly involved in multiple cheating cases linked to a construction venture, while Suresh had a history of property offences and alleged involvement in kidnapping-for-ransom cases.Two other accused, including alleged co-conspirator Srinivas Reddy, remain absconding as of Oct 17. Police are trying to trace them and recover the remaining ransom amount.
