articles.summary: Madhu Yaskhi Goud alleges Centre deleted 13 crore votes via SIR, impacting Dalits, Adivasis and minorities; urges unity to defend Constitution.

articles.title: Secular-minded voters targeted for deletion through SIR, says Goud
articles.summary: Telangana Congress chief B Mahesh Kumar Goud alleges BJP used SIR to delete secular voters from rolls, affecting Muslims, poor and adivasis.
articles.body: Hyderabad: Telangana Congress president B Mahesh Kumar Goud on Saturday accused the BJP of targeting secular-minded voters through the deletion of names from electoral rolls, alleging that a large number of voter names had been removed, with Muslims, the poor and adivasis accounting for a large proportion.In an informal interaction with media persons, Mahesh Goud alleged that the BJP raises the issue of foreign origins whenever it faces difficulties. He claimed that the BJP remained silent over alleged Chinese encroachments into Indian territory and accused the Modi govt of undermining constitutional institutions.He also alleged that nearly 97% of cases registered by the Enforcement Directorate were against industrialists affiliated with the opposition parties.Referring to the electoral roll issue, Goud said similar concerns had emerged in Musheerabad, where an FIR had been registered. articles.title: Truck smuggling UP paddy into Punjab intercepted at Dudhan Sadhan; FIR lodged
articles.summary: Punjab officials intercepted a truck smuggling undocumented UP paddy into Patiala at Dudhan Sadhan; FIR filed as crackdown targets illegal MSP claims.
articles.body: Patiala: Punjab Market Committee and food and civil supplies department officials intercepted a truck carrying undocumented PR paddy from Uttar Pradesh at Dudhan Sadhan interstate barrier around 7.40pm on Thursday. Police registered an FIR and took custody of the vehicle and its occupants.The action followed Punjab govt directives to prevent traders from bringing cheaper grain from other states into local mandis to claim MSP during the ongoing Kharif marketing season.The joint checking operation was conducted following directions from deputy general manager Rajnish Goel.Officials said Ramesh Lal, a resident of Ramana Ramani in Haryana’s Karnal district, was travelling with the driver. articles.title: Do not fear AI, understand it & adapt, TISS graduates told
articles.summary: TISS Hyderabad graduation: Prof YL Srinivas urges grads to embrace AI, be adaptable, and build knowledge in humanities; 173 students graduate.
articles.body: Hyderabad: India must move beyond being a practitioner to becoming a creator of knowledge in the humanities and social sciences, said Prof YL Srinivas, vice-chancellor of Sammakka Sarakka Central Tribal University, at the 12th annual graduation ceremony of Tata Institute of Social Sciences (TISS), Hyderabad, on Saturday. “Do not fear AI, understand it and remain adaptable,” he told the graduates at the ceremony held at National Academy of Agricultural Research Management (NAARM), Rajendranagar, urging them to contribute to the vision of Viksit Bharat.A total of 173 students from 20 states graduated across programmes in gender and development, rural development, cities and governance, public policy and governance, public policy and international relations, public policy and law, natural resources and governance, and doctoral studies in social sciences and women’s studies.Presenting the annual report, TISS Hyderabad campus director Prof Aseem Prakash said the campus offered nine master’s and four doctoral programmes and had 40 doctoral scholars. Women accounted for approximately half of the graduating cohort. The graduates included 37 from MA Public Policy and Governance, 28 from MA Natural Resources and Governance, 24 each from MA Cities and Governance and the dual-degree MA Public Policy and International Relations, 18 from MA Livelihoods: Rural Development, 15 from MA Public Policy and Law, nine each from MA Education and MA Livelihoods: Gender and Development, seven from the integrated MA Public Policy and Governance and LLM in Law and Social Policy, and two doctoral graduates each in Social Sciences and Women’s Studies.Prakash highlighted faculty publications, 77 invited lectures and the first Hyderabad Policy Conclave, which brought together 116 delegates across 26 sessions over three days. articles.title: In 2006, Bob Dylan and his brother bought a 25-acre Scottish estate for £2.2 million; after the pandemic kept them away, they sold the 16-bedroom property 17 years later for £4.26 million
articles.summary: American singer-songwriter Bob Dylan and his brother David Zimmerman sold their 25-acre Scottish Highlands estate for £4,257,650 in December 2023, nearly
articles.body: American singer-songwriter Bob Dylan and his brother David Zimmerman sold their 25-acre Scottish Highlands estate for £4,257,650 in December 2023, nearly doubling the £2.2 million they paid for it in 2006. According to STV News, the 16-bedroom Aultmore House was bought by whisky producer Angus Dundee Distillers after Dylan and his brother had not visited the property since the Covid-19 pandemic. The sale, reported by CoStar News in December 2023, ended the musician’s 17-year ownership of the historic mansion in Scotland’s Cairngorms National Park.A 16-bedroom mansion in the Scottish HighlandsLocated near Nethy Bridge in the Cairngorms National Park, Aultmore House is an A-listed Edwardian mansion surrounded by 25 acres of grounds. The property was listed for sale in July 2023, with offers invited above £3 million, according to reports citing estate agent Knight Frank.The main house has 16 bedrooms, 11 bathrooms and several reception rooms, including a music room. The wider estate includes cottages, a large greenhouse, a walled garden, a fountain, ornamental structures and a croquet lawn. The property also features a private, tree-lined driveway and views towards the Cairngorm mountains.According to CoStar News, the mansion was sold for £4.258 million to Angus Dundee Distillers, a whisky producer that owns Tomintoul Distillery in the Cairngorms and Glencadam Distillery in Brechin. Knight Frank handled the sale.The final price was significantly above the original asking threshold of £3 million. However, the sale price alone does not establish the sellers’ net profit, as it does not account for maintenance, improvements, transaction costs or other expenses incurred during their ownership.Why Dylan decided to sellDylan and Zimmerman bought Aultmore House in 2006 and reportedly visited it periodically over the years. However, the brothers had not returned since before the pandemic. Tom Stewart-Moore of Knight Frank said the property had been put on the market because it was “surplus to requirements”. The agent also indicated that the brothers had typically spent a few weeks there each year before the pandemic.Dylan had a longstanding musical association with the Scottish Highlands. His 1997 album 'Time Out of Mind' includes the song 'Highlands', a lengthy track that evokes the region’s landscape and the singer’s desire to return there. Dylan has also cited Scottish poet Robert Burns as an influence. In a 2008 HMV music campaign, he selected Burns’ poem 'A Red, Red Rose' among his inspirations. The musician received an honorary doctorate in music from the University of St Andrews in 2004.The property was therefore not simply a private residence. It had also been used as a holiday let and a venue for events. Its extensive grounds, multiple bedrooms and additional cottages made it suitable for accommodating guests.The sale followed a period in which the house had been marketed as a substantial country estate with potential for use as a private home or hospitality property. Angus Dundee Distillers’ purchase brought the mansion under new ownership, although the reported sale announcement did not detail the buyer’s plans for the property.A house with a history stretching back more than a centuryAultmore House predates Dylan’s ownership by nearly a century. It was built between 1911 and 1915 as a summer residence for Archibald Merrilees, an Aberdonian industrialist associated with the department-store business M&M in Russia.Merrilees reportedly spent only one summer at the house before his death in 1917. The property was sold in 1922 and later extended by the Nivinson family, who owned it for more than five decades.During the Second World War, the mansion was requisitioned for use as a convalescent home. In subsequent years, it served as a finishing school for foreign students and a bed-and-breakfast establishment. It later fell into disrepair before being purchased and restored around 2000, according to STV News.The building retains features associated with its period, including timber floors, decorative plasterwork and marble fireplaces.
